(Also, if this SCP is controlled by stories, why doesn't someone write a story where SCP-582 kills it's self? That would take care of it for good I think.) Better yet, they should write a story where SCP-582 kills SCP-682. Then both SCP's would be dealt with. That would be a cool fight to see.. 682 would win, but it would still be cool. item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I, like many others, notices the similarities to Creepypasta characters like Slendy as I was reading this. I was worried for a while that that's exactly what it was going to be. Instead, it's effectively a new, anomolous creepypasta that you have to keep the /r/nosleep fans from getting their hands on. I've actually considered using a similar idea before, where the collective consciousness of humans retroactively gives birth to the characters we create.

I loved the fact that it's been written in a bunch of different physical forms but because all the stories are linked, it still affects the SCP. I love that it's origin is a self-contained paradox. And I loves that some fan out there tried to write a "this isn't even my final form" end-of-the-world story before getting interrupted.

Imagine going to write a fictional story involving you as a character and by the time you're done writing it, it's no longer fictional and actually happened to you. -shudder-

…The reckoning had waited for this moment, the faces of thirteen men and women now gazing unmovingly at the shadowy entity at the floor before them. item.title: Dropping loot?
item.content:encoded:
On top of basic weaponization of the manifestations themselves; could it be written in the story that some sort of even took place which synthesized magical safes that can only be opened by SCP personal and contains very useful tools or artifacts for other uses (since attacking 582 would probably not end well), so that agents could later acquire the loot on the aftermath?

If they're gonna do that, it would probably be a good idea to make clear the events take place in very isolated places, and don't last very long, and preferably have as close to zero causalities as possible.

Of course, that's assuming authors actually have a choice when writing 582 stories.

item.title: Is it retrocausal, or does it compels the writers to write the future/guess stuff they didn't know?
item.content:encoded:
If the writer includes details they couldn't have know (say for example the contents of a safe) in a story that takes place in the future, does the contents of the safe change to match what was written? What if the author knows what is in the safe, and is instructed to write something else being inside? Or what if the contents of the safe is shown to the author, but then without their knowledge changed before the time the manifestation takes place?

Or if it's about an event in the past, what happens if a detail in the story makes it impossible for the story to be written in the first place? Or what if the author is aware of a fact about the place where the story took place that couldn't have been changed since the end of the story, but writes that at the end of the story it has changed (for example, there is a mountain there now, but the story says it has been flattened to ground level), what happens? And what if the author doesn't know, but is instructed to write something that is inconsistent with known reality by whoever is doing the instructions?
